name: 3.0 l inline six, naturally aspirated (reference engine)
_assumption: Generic modern 3.0 l NA inline six for learning purposes, not a specific production engine. Geometry from docs/plan.md iteration 2; all other values are estimates calibrated to the plausibility ranges in docs/research.md §10.
_displacement: Derived from bore and stroke: 6 * pi/4 * 0.084^2 * 0.090 = 2.993 l (plan.md says 2.998 l; geometry wins).
_assumption_conrodLength: Rod/stroke ratio 1.5, typical for passenger car engines.
_firingAngles: Crank angle of each cylinder's firing TDC (index 0 = cylinder 1), evenly spaced by 720/6 = 120 deg (research.md §1.2).

valveTiming_deg._reference: Crank angle after the cylinder's own firing TDC, 0..720 deg.
valveTiming_deg._assumption: Typical fixed cam timing without VANOS.

overrunFuelCut._assumption: Typical deceleration fuel cut: throttle closed and speed above enter_rpm cuts fuel; fuel returns below exit_rpm (above idle, so the engine does not stall) or when the throttle opens (research.md §3.3).

afterburn._assumption: research.md §2.10a: share of fuel still burning at EVO grows above 25 deg retard vs MBT (idle torque reserve is 20 deg and must not count), up to 60 % at 37 deg; half of it burns in the exhaust; catalyst follows the exhaust temperature with 10 s. Tuned assumptions [prüfen]. The catalyst starts warm (engine already driven), but below the light-off for pops.

drivetrain._assumption: Rear-wheel-drive saloon around the engine, research.md §8: 6-speed gearbox and final drive from §8.1, efficiency incl. differential, road load c_w*A and c_r from §8.2. The car stands on a road-load roller dyno that simulates its mass and road load (§8.4). Clutch capacity about 1.8x peak engine torque. Shift and clutch times are those of a quick driver with a sequential gearbox [prüfen].

_assumption_inertia: Crank train plus dual-mass flywheel, research.md §2.11 gives 0.15-0.25 kg m^2.

intake._assumption: Manifold volume incl. plenum and runners; throttle body size typical for 3.0 l.

combustion._assumption: research.md §2.6/§2.7/§2.10. indicatedEfficiencyBase at MBT and lambda 1; lambda factor is a parabola with its maximum at lambdaOptimum.

friction._assumption: Form of the Heywood correlation (research.md §2.8), fmep = c0 + c1*(N/1000) + c2*(N/1000)^2, but with lower coefficients for a modern low-friction engine. Calibrated so that bmep and peak power land in research.md §10. [prüfen]

_assumption_accessoryTorque: Alternator, water pump, oil pump drive (T_aux in research.md §2.9), taken as constant.

exhaust._assumption: Backpressure grows with the square of the exhaust mass flow: p_exh = p_amb + k * mdot^2, about +15 kPa at 0.2 kg/s.
exhaust._assumption_pipes: Pipe after each collector and the common pipe after the Y-piece (incl. muffler and tailpipe), typical lengths; used by the sound model (research.md §6.3).

_tables: Paths relative to shared/. ve, lambdaTarget and ignition are the ECU tune; ignitionMbt is a property of the engine model, not of the ECU.
